issues.reason: The loss is real — "always" leaves no trace and the sealed clause reads as unqualified — but the defect half falls: the Quantifiers section's own fallback for a frequency adverb with no slot ("leave the unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it") covers exactly this case, since a sealed conjunct carries no truth value for the strength channel and the companion's (QuantifierPhrase <kind> <verb-lemma> "<word>") has no licensed filler for the definite individual "the village" (the companion "only ever restates a range the rule itself quantifies — never a range that appears nowhere else in the parse", which bars the kind village).

gaps_confirmed: Frequency adverb on a habitual whose subject is a definite individual, not a kind: the QuantifierPhrase companion's first slot is a kind range the claim does not quantify, so "always" has no surface-record carrier.
Inside an attitude seal there is no truth value for the frequency dial to set, so the strength channel of the two-channel frequency rule is unavailable there.

Day-of-year dating ("day 68 of Year 1", no month): (Day <n>) is day-of-month and the seeded date-ordering rules key on year/month/day, so (Day 68) + (Year 1) is emittable but not interpretable as stated.
